focus: Chained slaves are marched through shifting geometry in obsidian corridors; the Nameless One witnesses a wall glyph change from "Obey" to "Choice" and connects with five observant slaves.

Not the natural volcanic glass that formed when lava cooled rapidly, but something engineered—polished to mirror-smoothness, reflecting distorted images of the chained procession that stumbled through its depths.
Dozens of Nameless Ones moved in a loose column, some supported by others, many weeping soundlessly, all struggling with bodies that responded poorly to commands still being learned.
Muscles tensed to obey before conscious thought could intervene.
The word rang through consciousness like a bell struck in silence.
Pain lanced through already-abused ankle joints.
But five—five specific individuals scattered through the column—had paused fractionally when the glyph changed.
They descended through levels that seemed to have no logical relationship to one another.
They moved with the inevitability of glaciers, patient and implacable and utterly devoid of mercy.
Many of the Nameless Ones stumbling through these corridors wouldn't survive their first shift.

The mining operation sprawled before them like a vision of methodical hell—tier upon tier of excavated stone descending into depths that disappeared into darkness despite the harsh illumination provided by floating light-spheres that drifted through the air like captured stars.

Reptilian Overseers moved among the workers like sharks through dark water, energy whips crackling in their clawed hands.

The five who had noticed the changing glyph were scattered through the new arrivals being processed into the mining operation, but the Nameless One felt their presence like distant stars—dim, but there.
The Reptilian guard yanked the chain one final time, pulling the Nameless One toward a tool station where crude implements waited.
The Nameless One's hands closed around the worn handle—the first tool they had ever held, the first object they had ever chosen to grip.
